IFL_2000_Caucasus.title: Caucasus Intact Forests 2000
IFL_2000_Caucasus.abstract: Extent of Intact Forest Landscapes (IFLs) in the Caucasus region in 2000. IFLs are large, continuous areas of natural ecosystems without significant human disturbance or fragmentation. The 2000 baseline supports comparison with later IFL assessments to track forest integrity, habitat connectivity, and conservation status across the Caucasus ecoregion.
IFL_2000_Caucasus.notes:
• Baseline Intact Forest Landscapes for year 2000.
  • Clipped to the Caucasus ecoregion extent from the global IFL product.
  • Compare with the 2013 IFL layer and the 2000–2013 difference layer.
IFL_2000_Caucasus.data_attribution: Intact Forest Landscapes Project, Transparent World, and Global Forest Watch.
IFL_2000_Caucasus.citation: Potapov, P. et al. Intact Forest Landscapes of the World (2000 baseline). Intact Forest Landscapes Project. https://www.intactforests.org.
IFL_2000_Caucasus.license_text: Please refer to the original data provider's terms of use and licensing conditions available at https://www.intactforests.org.

IFL_2013_Caucasus.title: Caucasus Intact Forests 2013
IFL_2013_Caucasus.abstract: Extent of Intact Forest Landscapes (IFLs) in the Caucasus region in 2013. Intact Forest Landscapes are large, continuous areas of natural ecosystems that show no significant signs of human activity or habitat fragmentation. The dataset provides an updated assessment of forest integrity across the Caucasus and serves as a reference for evaluating changes in forest condition, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem connectivity over time.
IFL_2013_Caucasus.notes:
• Intact Forest Landscapes (IFLs) are unfragmented natural ecosystems large enough to maintain native biodiversity and ecological processes.
  • The layer represents forest conditions in 2013.
  • IFL boundaries were derived from satellite imagery and ancillary environmental datasets.
  • The dataset supports assessments of forest integrity, habitat connectivity, and conservation planning.
  • This layer can be compared with the 2000 IFL dataset to identify areas of forest loss, fragmentation, or persistence.
IFL_2013_Caucasus.data_attribution: Intact Forest Landscapes Project, Transparent World, and Global Forest Watch.
IFL_2013_Caucasus.citation: Potapov, P., Yaroshenko, A., Turubanova, S., Hansen, M.C., et al. Intact Forest Landscapes of the World (2013 baseline). Intact Forest Landscapes Project. Available through https://www.intactforests.org.
IFL_2013_Caucasus.license_text: Please refer to the original data provider's terms of use and licensing conditions available at https://www.intactforests.org.

IFL_difference_2000_2013_Caucasus.title: Caucasus Intact Forests Difference 2000–2013

caucasus_glaciers.title: Caucasus Glaciers (RGI 6.0)
caucasus_glaciers.abstract: Glacier outlines for the Caucasus region from the Randolph Glacier Inventory (RGI) version 6.0.   • Caucasus subset compiled in the Sustainable Caucasus archive; not a substitute for the latest national glacier inventories.
  • Compare with GLIMS glacier polygons where multi-source validation is required.
